correctness.rationale: For every connected noncomplete strongly regular graph, the defining adjacency relation gives the exact \((zI+L)^{-1}\) in the proof. Jacobi complementary minors and differentiation at zero reduce each triple cost to one of four exact adjugate quotients. The three successive difference numerators are strictly positive for \(b\ge3,\mu\ge1\). The complementary-graph parameter split exhausts all possible minimum induced-edge types and exact counts. The embedded verification program checks matrix identities and grounded trace values for nine graph examples; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Unlike published universal joint-centrality/resistance formulas, the new result gives all four exact costs and proves universal strict ordering by induced triple edge count, then obtains parameter-only classification and multiplicities for optimal three-noise-free-leader placements on all connected noncomplete strongly regular graphs. No covering theorem was found in targeted publication and mathematical-record comparisons; general antecedent formulas remain an important proximity risk.
residual_risks: A general joint-centrality formula is an immediate antecedent; the specialized result must be valued for its algebraically proved optimal triple hierarchy and exhaustive count, not for an already-known all-graph performance framework.
Specialized work on grounded strongly regular graph Laplacian minors or three-leader selection might be unindexed or use different terminology.

value.rationale: The motivated control-design objective is the exact total follower variance with precisely three noiseless reference leaders. On the natural and often non-vertex-transitive strongly regular family, the theorem replaces combinatorial leader search and many inverse matrices with a closed form and an exact structural optimality trichotomy using only graph parameters. All admissible leader triple patterns and every optimum are classified and counted, with strictly positive cost gaps; this is not an arbitrary finite instance, a normalization check or a restatement of a general optimization routine.
